description: This pre-solicitation notice is to inform potential offerors that the Albany NY VA Medical Center will be posting a solicitation (36C24227B0006) on or about November 6th, 2026, to provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, and supervision necessary to complete the Consolidate Primary Care Reception project(528A8-22-814). This project includes the construction services for second part of the Consolidate Primary Care (CPC) projects phase 1 that will continue to consolidate the primary care units currently located on the 1st, 4th, and 8th floors in Building 1 of the Albany VA Medical Center campus: blue, red, and silver teams respectively along with all relevant and necessary functions. The three primary care units are being combined on the first-floor core of the Albany VAMC. Also included is the relocation of the Agent Cashiers office in the existing space. In this phase, a new reception area shall be built to accommodate six (6) Medical Support Assistants (MSA) desks and a waiting lobby at the Albany VA Medical Center 113 Holland Avenue, Albany NY 12208. It has been determined that there are qualified firms in accordance with Public Law 109-461 that are capable of performing under NAICS Code 236220, "COMMERCIAL AND INSTITUTIONAL BUILDING CONSTRUCTION", with a size standard of $45M. Therefore this procurement is 100% set-aside for Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses. The estimated construction value of this project is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. Information regarding the scheduled site visit will be stated in the Solicitation. Bid bonding will be required to respond to this IFB once released. OBTAINING SOLICITATION MATERIAL Solicitation materials consisting of the Information for Proposal Details, Specifications, Drawings and Contract Forms will be available on http://www.sam.gov in electronic format only. These should be available on or about November 6th, 2026. An Offeror's mailing list, list of interested parties and/or list of attendees at site visits WILL NOT be prepared nor distributed by the Contract Specialist. SOLICITATION AMENDMENTS: Amendments to the solicitation will be posted at http://www.sam.gov. Paper copies of the amendments will NOT be individually mailed. No other notification of amendments will be provided. Offerors are reminded that they are responsible for obtaining and acknowledging all amendments to this solicitation and attaching to their bid. All bids and correspondence will be by email only to the Contracting Officer: Michael.Spivack@va.gov.

title: France – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Solution SaaS - Programmation et optimisation des flux entrants du processus logistique
description: Le centre de services Logistique Industrielle (LI), rattaché à la Direction des Services Supports (DIR2S) d’Enedis souhaite se doter d'une solution SaaS clé en main, permettant la planification, l’optimisation, le pilotage et la traçabilité des flux de livraison en entrée des sites logistiques, au service de la performance opérationnelle des sites logistiques et de la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Au-delà des fonctions de planification, la solution devra constituer un véritable outil de pilotage de l’activité, en intégrant des capacités avancées d’analyse, de reporting et de valorisation des données. Elle doit permettre une vision consolidée, fiable et exploitable des flux de livraison fournisseur, à la fois à la maille de chaque site logistique et au niveau national, afin de faciliter la prise de décision, l’anticipation des charges et l’amélioration continue des processus. Montant maximum du marché : 869 000 € HT. Le présent marché est mono attributaire. 5 candidats maximum seront retenues pour participer à la phase de consultation. Durée ferme du marché: 3 ans. reconduction : 5 fois un an. La date de début du marché est estimée au : 26/04/2027.

title: France – Parts of railway or tramway locomotives or rolling stock; railways traffic-control equipment – Système de mesure automatisée des roues de tramway au défilé (SMAR) : fourniture, installation, mise en service et maintien en conditions opérationnelles, ligne T2 et lignes de tramway fer de la RATP
description: Le présent avis vise à mettre en place un marché mono-titulaire, non alloti, à minimum et maximum exprimés en quantités, exécuté par ordres de livraison et de service, ayant pour objet, pour chaque site équipé : la conception, la fourniture, l'installation et la mise en service d'un dispositif de mesure au défilé du profil des roues de tramway (capteurs laser, caméras, éclairage, armoire, modules de traitement et de communication) ; la fourniture, le paramétrage et la mise en service du logiciel de reconstruction et d'exploitation des profils de roues et son intégration au système d'information de maintenance de la RATP ; l'étude d'implantation et les prestations d'intégration sur l'infrastructure ; les essais, la validation métrologique et l'accompagnement d'une période probatoire de six mois ; la documentation en français et la formation des mainteneurs ; la garantie de trois ans à compter de la réception définitive, incluant la maintenance du dispositif et du logiciel ; la fourniture de pièces de rechange et la gestion de l'obsolescence (disponibilité garantie quinze ans) ; sur commande, la maintenance post-garantie. Minimum (engagement ferme) : équipement de la ligne T2, soit deux (2) dispositifs en voie de remisage des sites de maintenance et de remisage d'Issy-les-Moulineaux et de Colombes, avec le logiciel, la mise en service, la vérification de service régulier et la garantie de trois ans à compter de la réception définitive. Maximum : huit (8) dispositifs au total sur l'ensemble des lignes de tramway fer (T1, T2, T3a, T3b, T7, T8), le raccordement de cinq lignes supplémentaires au logiciel, la maintenance post-garantie des huit dispositifs et du logiciel jusqu'au terme du marché, la capacité de mesure des roues de 370 mm pour huit dispositifs (ligne optionnelle) et les prestations d'expertise technique, dans la limite des quantités maximales de l'article 17 du projet de marché. Les travaux préparatoires d'acheminement des réseaux et le génie civil sont réalisés par la RATP hors marché.

description: 27-RFP-ROICC-0008 - Gutter Cleaning and Maintenance Services at Naval Weapons Station Earle, Colts Neck, NJ This notice is being issued strictly for Market Research, information and planning and purposes only and shall not be construed as either a solicitation or obligation or commitment on the part of the Government. There will not be a solicitation, specifications, or drawings available at this time. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to help The Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC), Naval Weapons Station Earle (NWSE), understand industry best practices and sources capable of meeting the requirements detailed by this announcement. NWSE welcomes responses from all interested parties; however, no decision or award of contract will be made based on responses from industry. NWSE will not pay for the preparation of, nor the subsequent use of information submitted in response to this Sources Sought. Respondents will not be notified of the outcome of NWSE�s review of the information received. Requirement: The source of this requirement is NAVFAC, Naval Weapons Station (NWS) Earle Requirements Branch and the Facilities Services Branch, located in Colts Neck, NJ. The requirement is for Maintenance and Repair of Gutters and Downspouts Services at NWS Earle in Colts Neck, NJ. Contractor shall perform gutter maintenance to ensure proper gutter and down spout drainage operation during the year. The Contractor shall maintain gutters in proper condition and operation; gutters are properly pitched and correctly attached and draining away from the building; maintain gutters so they do not leak to include seams and corners; clean gutters removing debris and disposing of off station. Please submit responses by 6 November 2026 11:00AM EST directly to Joseph Henrius, Contracting Officer, via email at joseph.p.henrius.civ@us.navy.mil. title: GLQ and TDY apartment cleaning services
description: The U.S. Embassy in Madrid plans to issue Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. 19SP5027Q0002 for cleaning services. The work covers about 110 Government-leased apartments and single-family homes in central Madrid and its suburbs, plus one temporary duty (TDY) apartment. Services include cleaning leased residences before a new resident moves in, cleaning the TDY apartment after each guest leaves, and weekly touch-up cleaning of the TDY apartment during guest stays. The contractor will provide all labor, supervision, supplies and equipment, except for limited items the Government provides. The Government plans to award multiple firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts. Each contract will have a 12-month base period and three 12-month option periods. Prices will be in euros. The Government will award to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offerors that it finds responsible. Offerors must: Operate an established business with a permanent address and telephone listing in Madrid, Spain. Hold all licenses and permits required under Spanish law. Have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) before award. Show relevant past performance providing comparable services in Spain. Provide a Project Manager who understands written and spoken English. Carry the minimum insurance specified in the solicitation. The RFQ will be posted on SAM.gov about mid-November. description: 2 STATEMENT OF WORK/PWS Boss Retractor Instruments Veterans Affairs Health Care System Oklahoma City, Oklahoma General: Currently, the Oklahoma City Veterans Affairs Health Care System (herein after referred to as OKC VAHCS) Surgery Service requires one Globus Medical Complete Set instruments for Neuro and Ortho Spine surgeries in the OR. Delivery Location: Oklahoma City Veterans Affairs Health Care System, 921 N.E. 13th St. Oklahoma City, Ok 73104 Delivery Times: Delivery times shall be Monday through Friday from 07:00 to 16:00 (7:00AM to 4:00PM). Definitions/Acronyms OKC VAHCS: Oklahoma City Veterans Affairs Health Care System Scope: The Contractor will provide the necessary instrument system and trays to the OKC VAHCS for one (1) Globus Instrument Set. Additionally, the requirement is for a comprehensive and whole solution to the requirement. The Contractor is required to be an expert in the field of Neuro Spine/Ortho Spine. As such, the Contractor is required to include any items not specifically listed in the pricing schedule but is necessary to enable the equipment or accompanying software to function. title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: **Note: Amendment 0003 is hereby posted on 10/14. Only those whom submitted timely Volumes I-III are eligible to submit the remaining Volume IV** The sources sought originally posted as W912HP27RA001 - Due to technical issues with ACWS a new solicitation number was pulled. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 541350 (Building Inspection Services), with a small business size standard of $19.0 million. The Product Service Code (PSC) is H339. Requirement & Scope of Work The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), United States Penitentiary (USP) Atwater, intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for a certified Category 5 (Cat 5) Elevator Safety Test and Inspection. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, and certified expertise necessary to perform the full-rated load and speed safety testing (Cat 5) in strict compliance with ASME A17.1, state, and federal safety regulations. title: 9905--MD | KC VAMC | VHA SIGNAGE PROGRAMMING | (VA-27-00007248)
description: KCVA Signage Programming Manufacturing Installation GENERAL INFORMATION 1. Title of Project: KCVA Signage Programming 2. Scope of Work: Updated interior and exterior signs are needed in each building of the Kansas City VA Medical Center and on the exterior of the campus. The types of signage needed include wayfinding, identification, super graphics, and life safety. This phased project will consist of updates to and/or the creation of the following planning, audit, programming, design development solutions, execution/fabrication, and option years for completion of the phased planning. The awardee shall ensure that all signage, design, programming, fabrication, installation and de-installation fully comply with all applicable commercial, regulatory, safety, accessibility, and VA technical standards. This includes adherence to the VA Technical Information Library (TIL) Signage Guidelines, as well as compliance with national and universal life safety codes including the NFPA Life Safety Code. All signage must meet ADA accessibility standards for visual, tactile, Braille, mounting height and readability, and incorporate hospital-grade requirements. All branding, typography, color use, symbol usage, and graphic treatments shall align with the VA Graphic Style and Branding Strategy Guidelines. Signage materials, finishes, construction details, installation details, and durability requirements shall conform to the VA standards, including requirements for non-ligature signage in mental health areas, and compliance with Infection Control policies, safety procedures, and environment of care expectations. The contractor must ensure all signage meets applicable OSHA, IBC, ABAAS, JCAHO and VHA safety standards. NAICS: 339950, 238990, 541410, 541430 PSC: R599 or N099 SIZE STANDARD: 500 employees

title: E-6B Software Licenses for 2027
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-271 Airborne Strategic Command, Control and Communications Program Office, intends to enter into negotiations and subsequently award to Rockwell Collins, Inc., doing business as Collins Aerospace Government Systems Division (CAGE Code: 13499), a modification to Delivery Order (DO) N0001925F0087 issued under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0001924G0017, to procure one-year of Java SE, MySQL, Trellix, and Veeam software licenses required to support the Block I and Block II Mission Software System, Sustainment and Support System (SASS), and Command Display Unit (CDU) for the E-6B aircraft for 01 December through 30 November 2027. The software licenses are required to operate the systems listed above. This action is anticipated to be greater than SAT. This action is not subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) and/or a Free Trade Agreement (FTA). This action is not anticipated to be awarded as a construction contract to a small business. This action does not require qualification requirements to be eligible for award. BOA N0001924G0017 was awarded sole source to Collins Aerospace under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1 prior to the Department of War implementation of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Part 6, Class Deviation (CD) 2026-O0017, Revision 1, dated 23 January 2026. The modification for software licenses described above will be on an existing delivery order for highly specialized software support services, on the systems identified above, related to mission system installation, operation, sustainment, development, integration, and testing on the E-6B aircraft for which Collins Aerospace is the Original Equipment Manufacturer. As such, Collins Aerospace possesses the technical data and knowledge, including system architecture and compatibility requirements for Block I and Block II Mission Software System, SASS, and CDU on the E-6B aircraft, which are necessary to identify the quantity and version of the required software licenses for those systems. Award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Any technical data associated with this action can be obtained through Rockwell Collins Inc. description: See Soliciation Amendments 0001 and 0002. USAISR's Combat Casualty Care Research Team 1 (CRT-1) requires resupply of its Blood Donor Room on a reoccurring basis in order to satisfy research requirements for blood collection. Requirement & Scope of Work The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), United States Penitentiary (USP) Atwater, intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for a certified Category 5 (Cat 5) Elevator Safety Test and Inspection. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, and certified expertise necessary to perform the full-rated load and speed safety testing (Cat 5) in strict compliance with ASME A17.1, state, and federal safety regulations. Any missing tools will result in an immediate facility lockdown. Contraband: Cell phones, personal electronics, cameras, weapons, and drugs are strictly prohibited. title: E-6B Mission Computer Modernization (MCM) Software Licenses for Fiscal Year (FY) 27 and FY 28
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-271 Airborne Strategic Command, Control and Communications Program Office, intends to enter into negotiations and subsequently award to Rockwell Collins, Inc., doing business as Collins Aerospace Government Systems Division (CAGE Code: 13499), a modification to Delivery Order (DO) N0001925F0087 issued under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0001924G0017, to procure one (1) base year and one (1) option year of AGI Dynamic Geometry, Java SE, Jboss, MySQL, and Crossover software licenses required to support Mission Computer Modernization (MCM) efforts on the E-6B aircraft. The base licensing period will cover from 13 November 2026 through 12 November 2027, and the option licensing period will cover from 13 November 2027 through 12 November 2028. The software licenses are required to operate the system listed above. This action is anticipated to be greater than SAT. This action is not subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) and/or a Free Trade Agreement (FTA). This action is not anticipated to be awarded as a construction contract to a small business. This action does not require qualification requirements to be eligible for award. BOA N0001924G0017 was awarded sole source to Collins Aerospace under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1 prior to the Department of War implementation of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Part 6, Class Deviation (CD) 2026-O0017, Revision 1, dated 23 January 2026. The modification to procure the software licenses described above will be executed under an existing delivery order N0001925F0087. The existing order requires Collins Aerospace to provide software support services related to mission system installation, operation, sustainment, development, integration, and testing on the E-6B aircraft systems for which Collins Aerospace is the Original Equipment Manufacturer, including the MCM. As such, Collins Aerospace possesses the technical data and specialized knowledge, including system architecture and compatibility requirements for the MCM, which is necessary to identify the exact version and quantity of software licenses required to support and operate that system. Award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Any technical data associated with this action can be obtained through Collins Aerospace. This action is a result of the sources sought notice posted on 28 July 2026. This action will not be a small business set aside. The NAVAIR Office of Small Business Programs concurs with this set-aside determination. The National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research (NIDCR), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), intends to negotiate and award a sole source purchase order to Johns Hopkins University for Rheumatologist Services for the NIDCR Dental Clinic. Proposed Contractor: Johns Hopkins University Contact: Kevin Stark, Sr. Grants and Contracts Analyst Email: kstark3@jhmi.edu Telephone: (410) 550-8510 Fax: (410) 550-2072 DUNS: 00-191-0777 UEI: FTMTDMBR29C7 The Government anticipates award under the authority of FAR 13.501(a) and FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. No solicitation package is available. Any responsible source that believes it is capable of meeting this requirement may submit a capability statement by the closing date of this notice. The Government will consider all timely capability statements solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Requirement NIDCR has a continuing requirement for a part-time Rheumatologist to support the Dental Clinical Resource Core (DCRC) and the Salivary Gland Disorders research team. The contractor shall provide clinical, research, and training support related to Sjogren�s syndrome and other rheumatologic conditions with oral manifestations, including: clinical expertise supporting research of human subject protocols, amendments, and adverse event reporting; clinical management and evaluation of patients/subjects with rheumatologic conditions associated with salivary gland pathology; participation in screening and enrollment of subjects to clinical research protocols; support to the NIDCR Dental Clinic two days per week, with one day on-site and one day off-site; and participation in research analysis, publications, presentations, and collaborative activities. The contractor shall perform these services for 832 hours annually. Minimum qualifications include: medical degree and preferably board certification in rheumatology; active U.S. medical license in good standing; extensive publication record in Sjogren�s syndrome and rheumatologic conditions with oral manifestations; and active collaboration with a dental clinical research team in salivary gland disorders. Sole Source Justification Johns Hopkins University is the only known source capable of providing the required specialized rheumatology expertise, clinical research support, and collaborative experience necessary to support the NIDCR Salivary Gland Disorders research program. The proposed source has the unique capability to provide a rheumatologist with demonstrated expertise in Sjogren�s syndrome and related rheumatologic conditions with oral manifestations, along with the ability to support ongoing clinical care, protocol development, subject enrollment, research collaboration, and training activities integral to the NIDCR mission. Award to another source would result in unacceptable delays, duplication of effort, and increased programmatic risk. description: Sources Sought Fort Leavenworth Underground Fuel Tank Testing Services INTRODUCTION The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for Underground Fuel Tank Testing and Maintenance on Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. title: ISBEE Solicitation: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal healthcare services for Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) services equivalent to two full-time CNMs at Rosebud Service Unit, Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota.
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION � CERTIFIED NURSE-MIDWIFE SERVICES RFP No. 75H70627R00005 The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) healthcare services at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. This requirement is set aside for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) under NAICS 561320, Temporary Help Services. The Contractor shall provide qualified CNM personnel sufficient to support two (2) full-time CNM positions providing outpatient obstetric, gynecological, prenatal, postpartum, family planning, and women�s primary care services, as well as obstetric emergency on-call coverage for the Emergency Department. The anticipated contract will use a Firm-Fixed-Price, Month-of-Service (MOS) pricing structure. One MOS represents complete monthly performance of the required CNM services in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The anticipated period of performance consists of a three (3)-month base period and three (3) option periods of three (3) months each, for a maximum potential period of performance of twelve (12) months. Services will be performed primarily at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. Standard outpatient clinic hours are generally Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The requirement also includes shared 24-hour-per-day, 7-day-per-week CNM on-call availability for obstetric emergencies during non-clinic hours. Offerors shall provide qualified personnel meeting the education, certification, licensure, credentialing, privileging, background investigation, health, and other qualification requirements identified in the PWS. The Government intends to make award to the responsible Offeror whose proposal conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the best value to the Government, price and other factors considered. Evaluation factors include Technical Capability, Past Performance, Management Approach, and Price. Applicable provisions and clauses, including FAR 52.212-1, FAR 52.212-2, FAR 52.212-4, and applicable FAR/HHSAR requirements, are incorporated by reference or provided in the solicitation and attachments. Prospective Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation, PWS, price schedule, and all attachments prior to submission. Proposals are due November 6, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CT.

Contractor shall provide all necessary facilities, materials, equipment, and personnel to perform DOCKSIDE repairs to the U.S. Coast Guard Cutter (USCGC) RELIANCE (WMEC 615). The vessel is home ported in Pensacola, FL. All work will be performed at the cutter home port. There is no geographical restriction for this cutter. This work will include, but is not limited to the following Work Items: WORK ITEM 1: Flexible Couplings, Renew WORK ITEM 2: Seawater Heat Exchangers, Clean, Inspect And Hydro WORK ITEM 3: Boiler Exhaust Stack Uptakes, Commercial Clean WORK ITEM 4: Lube Oil Heat Exchangers; Clean, Inspect And Hydro WORK ITEM 5: Chill Water System, Clean and Flush WORK ITEM 6: Boilers, Renew WORK ITEM 7: Potable Water Pneumatic Tanks, Clean and Inspect WORK ITEM 8: Hot Water Accumulator Tanks, Clean and Inspect WORK ITEM 9: Steering Gear, General, Overhaul WORK ITEM 10: Sewage Discharge and Vacuum Pumps, Renew WORK ITEM 11: Grey Water Holding Tanks, Clean and Inspect WORK ITEM 12: Sewage Holding Tanks, Clean and Inspect WORK ITEM 13: Sewage Piping, Clean and Flush WORK ITEM 14: Tanks, Grey Water Holding, Preserve, 100 percent WORK ITEM 15: Temporary Services, Heating and Cooling WORK ITEM 16: Tanks (Sewage Holding), Preserve, Partial � OPTION ITEM WORK ITEM 17: Fire and Smoke Thermal Detector Sensors, Renew WORK ITEM 18: Reduction Gear Lube Oil Strainer Assembly, Replace WORK ITEM 19: Galley Deck Plating, Renewal WORK ITEM 20: Exhaust Piping, Renew WORK ITEM 21: Seawater Piping and Thermometer, Renew WORK ITEM 22: Deck Plating, Renew WORK ITEM 23: Shore Connections, Renew WORK ITEM 24: Bulkhead Plating, Renew WORK ITEM 25: Deck Drain Piping, Renew WORK ITEM 26: Tank, Dirty Oil, Open and Clean WORK ITEM 27: Watertight Scuttle, External, Renew WORK ITEM 28: Sewage Piping, Renew WORK ITEM 29: Propulsion Shafting, Strain Gauge Alignment, Dockside, Check ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The period of performance is anticipated to be for fifty-six (56) calendar days with a start date of May 18, 2027 and end date of July 12, 2027. (Subject to change at the discretion of the Government) ANTICIPATED NAICS CODE/SIZE STANDARD: The applicable NAICS Code is 336611, Ship Building and Repairing and the size standard is 1,300 employees. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: Companies having capabilities necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements are invited to provide information to contribute to this market survey/sources sought notice including commercial market information and company information. Companies may respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Kaity.George@uscg.mil or via fax to (757) 628-4562 (Attn: Kaity George/C&P1-MEC) no later than 1:00 pm on Friday, November 6th, 2026, Eastern Standard Time (EST) with the following information/documentation: 1. Name of Company, Address and UEI Number. 2. Point of Contact and Phone Number. 3. Business Size applicable to the NAICS Code: 8(a) Small Business Concern; b. HubZone Small Business Concern; c. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (SDVOSBC); d. Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (VOSBC); e. ED Woman Owned Small Business Concern (EDWOSB); f. Woman Owned Small Business Concern (WOSBC); g. Small Business Concern; h. Large Business Concern 4. Documentation Verifying Small Business Certification: a. If claiming 8(a) status, provide a copy of your 8(a) Certificate from SBA. b. If claiming HuBZone status, provide a copy of your HuBZone Certificate from SBA. c. If claiming SDVOSBC status, provide documentation that shows the Service Disable Veteran (SDV) unconditionally owns 51 % of the business, controls the management and daily operations, and holds the highest officer position in the company. Documentation should also be provided to show that the SDV has a service-connected disability that has been determined by the Department of Defense or Department of Veteran Affairs. Finally, provide documentation that shows the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. d. If claiming VOSBC status, provide documentation that shows the Veteran unconditionally owns 51% of the business, controls the management and daily operation, make long-term decisions for the business, and holds the highest officer position in the company that works at the business fulltime during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. e. If claiming EDWOSB status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned by one or more women who are �economically disadvantaged�, and primarily managed by an economically disadvantaged woman that make long-term decisions for the business, hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full-time during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. A woman is presumed economically disadvantaged if she has a personal net worth of less than $750,000 (with some exclusions), her adjusted gross yearly income averaged over the three years preceding the certification less than $350,000, and the fair market value of all her assets is less than $6 million f. If claiming Woman Owned Small Business status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more women, and primarily managed by one or more women that make long-term decisions for the business and hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full time during normal working hours. The women must be U.S. citizens. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. g. If claiming Small Business status, provide documentation to show the business is small under NAICS code 336611. 5. Statement of Proposal Submission: Statement on how your company will do the work and that your company WILL submit a proposal as a prime contractor if a solicitation is issued as a result of this Sources Sought Notice. 6. Past Performance Information: Evidence of experience in work similar in type and scope to include contract numbers, project titles, and dollar amounts, points of contact and telephone numbers. If two companies are planning to conduct business and submit an offer as a Joint Venture or similar type of teaming agreement, they are requested to provide past performance information on projects of similar scope that they have performed together as a Joint Venture, if available. Providing individual past performance documentation from each company on separate projects where the two did not work together may be considered less relevant. title: Intent to Sole Source: AFIT - High Finesse WS8-2 Wavemeter
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The United States Air Force, AFLCMC/PZIBA, Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio 45433-5344 publishes this notice of intent to award a sole source contract for informational purposes only. This proposed action is for the acquisition of a wavemeter for the Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) located at Wright Patterson AFB, Ohio 45433. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(b), �One responsible source. Agencies may contract without providing for full and open competition when the supplies or services required by the agency are available from only one responsible source and no other type of supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements,� resulting in a firm fixed price contract. The reason for lack of competition is as follows: The proposed vendor, Toptica Photonics Inc., is the only known source able to satisfy the Government's requirements. No other vendor has developed a wavemeter to the precision of Toptica's WS8-2. The primary factor in choosing this wavemeter is its capability to reliably measure a wavelength to <2 MHz. Other companies produce wavemeters that can be as low as 20 MHz in precision, but only Toptica guarantees accuracy down to 2 MHz. For this reason Toptica is the only company that meets all of the requirements. Both AFIT and contracting personnel utilized subject matter experts with experience for this requirement and vendor outreach but were unable to find other resources that were able to meet this requirement. The Contracting Officer has determined that only one source is reasonably available: Toptica Photonics Inc. This proposed procurement will be a Sole Source under North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a size standard of 1000 employees. The proposed source is TOPTICA PHOTONICS INC, 1120 Pittsford Victor RD, Pittsford, New York,14534-3818, United States. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, quotation, or exception to the intent to purchase on a sole source basis, which shall be considered by the Government if received within five (5) days of this notice. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Department of Defense (DoD) has determined the System for Award Management (SAM) to be the single DoD registration for contractors who conduct business or who are interested in conducting business with the DoD. Contractors must be registered in SAM prior to award for contracts issued after 29 May 2012. You may contact SAM at 866-606-8220. SAM website: www.SAM.gov. The contact for this acquisition is Dametria Walder. Any information should be e-mailed to dametria.walder@us.af.mil no later than 1:00 pm Local (Wright-Patterson AFB) Time, Friday, 06 November 2026. Only inquiries/information received by this date will be considered. Be advised that all correspondence sent via e-mail shall contain a subject line that reads �FA860127Q0014 AFIT - High Finesse WS8-2 Wavemeter.� Note that e-mail filters at Wright-Patterson AFB are designed to filter e-mails without subject lines or with suspicious subject lines or contents (i.e., .exe, or .zip files). Therefore, if this subject line is not included, the e-mail may not get through the e-mail filters. Also, be advised that .zip or .exe files are not allowable attachments and may be deleted by the e-mail filters at Wright-Patterson AFB. If sending attachments with e-mail ensure only .PDF, .doc, or .xls documents are sent. The e-mail filter may delete any other form of attachments. description: Solicitation No.: 09242026 Agency: Federal Bureau of Prisons Project: FCC Yazoo City FY27 Grease Trap Maintenance and Cleaning Title: Amendment 0001 � Revision to Licensing Requirements 1. PURPOSE OF AMENDMENT This amendment revises the licensing requirement for offerors responding to Solicitation 09242026. The original solicitation required: �The prime contractor must be fully licensed and permitted by the State of Mississippi. Any subcontractor performing work must also be certified.� Market research and proposal evaluation revealed that no small business primes currently hold the required Mississippi licenses, creating an unintended barrier to competition in a Total Small Business Set?Aside. Accordingly, the Government is amending the solicitation to allow licensed subcontractors to satisfy the technical licensing requirement. This amendment is issued under the authority of: FAR 15.206(e) (Amendment of solicitations) FAR 14.404?1(c)(1) and (2) (Nonresponsive bids and insufficient competition) 2. REVISED LICENSING REQUIREMENT (REPLACES PRIOR TEXT) New Licensing Clause �The prime contractor OR the subcontractor(s) performing regulated grease trap pumping, waste removal, transport, or disposal activities must hold all licenses, permits, and certifications required by the State of Mississippi, including but not limited to: � MSDH Certified Pumper License � Mississippi solid waste hauling permits � Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) disposal authorization Copies of all licenses relied upon for compliance must be submitted with the offer.� Clarifications The entity performing the regulated activity must hold the license(s). The prime contractor is not required to personally hold Mississippi pumping or hauling licenses, provided that: A subcontractor performing the licensed portions of work holds all required licenses, and A signed letter of commitment is included in the proposal. The prime contractor retains full responsibility for management, oversight, and contract compliance. 3. SOLICITATION CHANGES � COMPETITION IMPACT This amendment is considered material. As required by FAR: A. The solicitation is hereby reopened. B. All offerors may revise and resubmit proposals. C. A new proposal due date will be established by separate notice. The Government determined under FAR 10.002 that the revised requirement continues to meet the agency�s minimum needs while enabling competition. 4. OFFER SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS (UPDATED) Due 11/6/26 12 Noon EST. Offerors relying on subcontractor licensing must submit: Copies of all applicable Mississippi licenses Proof of subcontractor commitment (signed letter or subcontract agreement) Identification of which entity (prime or subcontractor) will perform which regulated activities Failure to provide the above documentation will result in an �Unacceptable� rating for the Licensing compliance factor. 5. ALL OTHER TERMS AND CONDITIONS REMAIN UNCHANGED.

title: Tybee Island Shoreline Protection Project
description: This presolicitation is for the Tybee Island Shoreline Protection Project. This acquisition is being offered as an unrestricted full and open competitive solicitation and will result in a single Firm Fixed- Price Contract Award. The construction magnitude for this project is between $10,000,000.00 and $25,000,000.00. Description of Work: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District, intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) to award a single firm fixed-price contract. Project work consists of placing dredged material along the Front Beach at Tybee Island, Georgia. The Contract includes a Base Bid item and Optional Bid items. The Base Bid item consists of placing berm fill material along approximately 7,000 feet of the construction baseline. Optional Bid items include placing additional material along the Front Beach area. The berm width varies along the project length. The Base Bid quantity is approximately 820,000 cubic yards of material and the four Option Bid items consist of approximately 673,000 cubic yards of material to be dredged for this renourishment. The material for the project will be sourced from an approved offshore borrow area that is approximately 5,000 feet away from the south end of the project and 11,000 feet from the center of the project. Work also includes environmental restrictions and beach tilling. The total construction duration for this project is 90 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). Evaluation Criteria: The contract will be solicited and procured using FAR Part 14 Sealed Bidding Procedures. Note: The Government anticipates issuing the invitation for bids on or after 06 November 2026. This date is estimated and subject to change. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be made available through the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/. Interested parties are encouraged to register as an interested vendor on SAM.gov to receive notifications of solicitation amendments. The Government is not responsible for notifying interested parties who have not registered or otherwise monitored SAM.gov for updates. Prospective bidders must be registered in SAM.gov at the time of bid submission and maintain an active registration through contract award, in accordance with FAR 52.204-7. The only authorized transmission method for a bid in response to this solicitation is electronically via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. NO OTHER TRANSMISSION METHODS (EMAIL, FACSIMILE, REGULAR MAIL, HAND CARRIED, ETC.) WILL BE ACCEPTED. The bids must be received by the Government by the date/time specified in the solicitation. Bidders shall submit their bid via the PIEE website Solicitation Module using the following link: https://piee.eb.mil/. Instructions on how to submit a bid can be found using the following link https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/sol/Posting_Offer.pdf. Contractual Questions should be forwarded to Contract Specialist, MSG Jeffrey Francisco at jeffrey.o.francisco.@usace.army.mil or to the attention of the Contracting Officer, Mr. Preston Jones at preston.e.jones@usace.army.mil.

title: Kitchen Equipment
description: THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

Step One: A Pre-solicitation Notice will not be submitted separately, as this notice will be encompassed together with the Request for Quotation and released in SAM.gov. The website for SAM is https://www.sam.gov. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial supplies prepared in accordance with the format in FAR RFO 12.202, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes only the solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a formal solicitation will NOT be issued. An annual synopsis for requirements falling under the scope of this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will NOT be released in SAM.gov, despite any emergent requirements that may arise throughout the years. Attachment 0001 � Scope of Work Portfolio - Lumber BOA lists the lumber products to be ordered against this BOA, however, it is not limited to the list provided. Specific evaluation criteria for specific requirements shall be communicated with each BOA Delivery Order. The Offeror must demonstrate the capability to deliver, at a minimum, the specified lumber requirements to at least one (1) of the seven (7) military installations designated in this solicitation. Material MAY be inspected through the Government Quality Assurance (QA) Department. This will be determined at each Delivery Order level. The contractor MAY BE REQUIRED TO provide a Certificate of Conformance (COC) and Certified Test Report for all processes indicating contractor compliance with all associated tech data requirements. This will be determined at each Delivery Order level. The solicitation and incorporated provisions and clauses included in the resulting BOA master agreements are incorporated under Attachment 0002 and are in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 and made a part of each Government delivery order under the BOA. If any clauses are revised during the life of this BOA, the most recently dated version of the clause shall apply. The NAICS code for this procurement is 321113 (Sawmills). The small business standard for this NAICS is 550 employees. The Product Service Code is 5510 (Lumber). The Government will execute no-cost BOAs to offerors whose quotations in response to those solicitations are found acceptable on the criteria stated in the RFQ. The BOAs will be valid for a period of up to five (5) years beginning from the effective date of the initial BOA execution. NOTE: This BOA RFQ will be the only opportunity contractors have to obtain an executed Lumber BOA award to propose on Delivery Order RFQs issued within the next five (5) years. BOA quotations will not be solicited, accepted, and will not be executed at any other time, even for those emergent requirements not specifically identified in the initial synopsis. Therefore, if a contractor desires to participate in ANY future Lumber delivery order that may arise within the next five (5) years, it is imperative that the contractor submit a quotation in response to this Rigging BOA RFQ. The non-availability of raw materials, sub quoter issues, scheduling conflicts, etc. are not acceptable excuses for failing to meet the delivery schedules. Early delivery may be authorized but must be approved and coordinated in advance of due date with the contract specialist and contracting officer designated in each Delivery Order. If there is going to be a delay in delivery, the offeror is required to notify the contract specialist and contracting officer designated in the Delivery Order within 24 hours of knowledge of that delay. SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION ATLANTIC INTRACOASTAL WATERWAY DISPOSAL AREA 60
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION ATLANTIC INTRACOASTAL WATERWAY DISPOSAL AREA 60, ONSLOW COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information only. This is NOT a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. This request does not obligate the Government in any contract award. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Wilmington District, is conducting research to determine the market capabilities of potential contractors to perform a subsurface investigation for the purpose of collecting soil and strength parameters for the existing dike and foundation soils to complete slope stability analysis for the existing dike foundation soils. Disposal Area (DA) 60 is approximately 20 acres in size and located one and a quarter mile southeast of the NCWRC Cedar Point Boat Ramp, located in Cedar Point, North Carolina. Description of Services. The Contractor shall mobilize all necessary personnel, equipment, and materials to DA 60, to conduct a comprehensive geotechnical investigation. Methods of investigation should accurately locate changes in the soil strata. Equipment shall be able to traverse the site in wet, soft, or dry conditions. The following subsurface exploration and laboratory testing services will be required. Cone Penetration Test Sounding A total of eleven (11) CPT soundings shall be completed to a depth of 50 feet or refusal that occurs greater that 20 feet in depth, both within the crest of the existing dike structure, the interior of the existing dike structure, and waterside toe of the DA to assess soil stratigraphy and engineering properties. All work shall be completed in accordance with applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements, and coordinated with USACE representatives throughout the duration of the investigation. The Contractor shall be fully responsible for the transportation of all personnel, equipment, and materials to and from DA 60 for the duration of the geotechnical investigation. DA 60 is only accessible by water vessel; therefore, the Contractor must make all necessary arrangements for marine transportation to support field operations. No land access is available. 2. Site Information. Site maps, navigation charts and bathymetric maps may be acquired from the Wilmington District, Navigation Section. Historical tide data can be acquired from the NOAA Tides and Currents website; https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepredictions.html?id=8665728. Borehole coordinates will be provided by the Wilmington District for navigational purposes. 3. Water Vessel Requirements. All waterborne vessels shall be compliant with established US Coast Guard guidelines and regulations. 4. Field Work. As previously stated, this contract requires eleven (11) CPT soundings be conducted. All interested firms with 541360 as an approved NAICs code have until 6 November 2026 at 1500 ET to submit the following information: - Name & Address of your Firm - Point of Contact (Name/Phone/E-mail) - Current SAM - Business Size, to include designation as HUBZone, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Woman-Owned Business, and Large Business. Any supporting documentation that confirms your socio-economic status should be provided, i.e., letter of certification from VA confirming SDVOSB status. The Government must be able to verify SBA certification of HubZone and 8(a) via SAM. - Evidence of capabilities to perform comparable subsurface investigation work. The contractor must provide evidence of comparable work on two (2) recent projects (not more than seven (7) years old.) Include the project name and description of the key/salient features of the project (completion date, total contract value, and your company's level of involvement in the project, i.e., subcontractor (type), prime, GC, etc. and your specific role. Additionally, if you were teaming with another firm, clearly identify your role on the project(s) submitted. Please provide at least one point of contact (with e-mail address and phone number) for project validation. The Government will not give credit to projects if the lack of information hinders the ability to determine relevancy and/or level or experience. - Documentation of a drill rig that can perform CPT soundings as specified. The CPT equipment shall be pushed into the ground at a rate of 0.8 in/s. The CPT shall consist of a conical tip at the base of the rod for measuring the cone resistance and friction resistance every 0.8-inch interval. The cone shall have a base area of 1.6 in2, with a diameter of 1.4 in., and a height of 1.2 in., corresponding to a 60? apex angle. The cone is attached to a friction sleeve having a diameter of approximately 1.4 in. The tip of the cone is typically instrumented to measure the tip resistance using strain gauges, while the sleeve above the cone is instrumented to measure the sleeve friction. These parameters shall be used to obtain a profile of the variation of soil strength and soil type with depth. Additional instrumentation shall be attached to the cone to obtain additional data for correlation with other parameters such as porewater pressure. - Firm's capability to perform, to include geographic span and project size. - Information on Teaming Arrangement (if applicable). Although we are not looking for formal signed agreements at this time, if you intend to "team" with another firm, formally or informally, you must submit information, not more, than one (1) page, about your team's involvement. More specifically, you must submit sufficient information for the Government to determine the roles each team member will play and what your socio-economic status is or will be considering the proposed arrangement. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4(a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), is conducting market research to inform a planned future acquisition. The intent is to gather information from qualified solution providers offering solutions to meet this critical business need. The Government seeks industry input on a modern, modular, cloud-based system capable of supporting the coding staff to collect health care data and accurately applying the codes to determine level of care provided to the patient population and ensure timely coding and revenue cycle activities on behalf of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). This notice is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It shall not be construed as an Invitation for Bid, Request for Quotation, or Request for Proposal. This RFI does not commit the Government to any acquisition or contract award. Respondents will not be compensated for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information. No funds have been authorized or obligated for this requirement. All submissions become Government property. Respondents are responsible for marking proprietary information. VA does not want this market research to assume that today's current solution should simply be carried forward. VA is specifically seeking industry's perspective on how modern technology can meet the ability to provide this auditing, billing and coding capability across VHA. VA seeks industry feedback to inform future acquisition strategies for an enterprise-wide Healthcare Data Auditing Billing and Coding Optimization Software that enhances decision making, efficiency, supports VA coding professionals the ability to accurately and consistently code health care encounters and inpatient stays. Responses may support potential socioeconomic set-aside determinations; therefore, submissions should be complete, detailed, and accurate. Desired Outcomes Improve the accuracy, timeliness, consistency, and traceability of coding and billing activities. Provide configurable workflows for coding, clinical documentation integrity, billing, utilization review, compliance, and supervisory functions. Enable secure, standards-based, near-real-time or real-time exchange with Government clinical, scheduling, billing, identity, analytics, and enterprise data services. Provide enterprise, regional, facility, workgroup, and user-level reporting with auditable metrics. Reduce avoidable manual work, duplicate data entry, proprietary dependencies, and lifecycle cost. Maintain continuity of operations, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and records-management compliance. Capability Requirements Enterprise Platform and User Experience An enterprise-capable solution or interoperable suite available to authorized users across geographically distributed facilities. Role-based access, configurable menus, work queues, dashboards, alerts, and administrative controls. A coherent user experience across coding, documentation integrity, billing, compliance, workflow, and reporting functions, while allowing modular components when beneficial. Support for large user populations and workload growth without per-user barriers that discourage adoption. Accessibility consists of applicable Federal information and communication technology requirements and compatibility with common assistive technologies. Coding and Encounter Management Support identification, assignment, review, coding, recoding, completion, and tracking of inpatient, outpatient, surgical, emergency, behavioral health, long-term care, and other encounters. Support current diagnosis, inpatient procedure, professional procedure, supply, dental, and other applicable code sets, including effective-date validation and version management. Validate code relationships, age, clinical attributes, modifiers, provider data, coverage, medical necessity, payer rules, and Government-configurable edits. Support code lookup and integration with one or more coding reference or encoder products through documented interfaces. Maintain status, assignment, reassignment, comments, communications, original values, changed values, user identity, reason, and date-time audit history. Clinical Documentation Integrity Provide independent, role-appropriate work queues for concurrent and retrospective review. Identify potential documentation improvement opportunities using configurable criteria and transparent logic. Create, route, communicate, and track documentation clarification requests and responses. Capture documentation-review codes, grouping results, severity, risk, expected length of stay, quality indicators, and comparison with final coded outcomes where applicable. Provide workload, response, impact, quality, and productivity reporting for documentation integrity programs. Billing, Claim Editing, and Compliance Provide institutional and professional claim review before and, where needed, after submission. Apply national, local, payer, technical, coding, medical necessity, provider identifier, present-on-admission, grouping, sequencing, and Government-defined edits. Support individual and batch claim review, transparent edit explanations, configurable messages, and authorized maintenance of custom rules. Identify incomplete, duplicate, non-billable, held, cancelled, retrospective-insurance, and same-day related encounters and preserve supporting rationale. Provide random and targeted sampling, compliance monitoring, complete audit trails, and exportable review results. Workflow and Auditability Provide configurable work assignment, prioritization, routing, escalation, suspense, alerts, and closure across organizational levels. Enable secure communication among coding, documentation integrity, billing, clinical, utilization review, compliance, supervisory, and technical personnel. Maintain tamper-evident or otherwise trustworthy audit history for user, system, rule, integration, and administrative actions. Permit authorized users to configure workflows and rules without vendor software development when feasible. Expose workflow data through documented interfaces and export mechanisms. Integration and Data Exchange Support bidirectional integration with the VistA electronic health record, legacy clinical, scheduling, admissions/discharge/transfer, surgery, clinical documentation, imaging report, laboratory, radiology, procedure, provider, identity, billing, and enterprise data services. Use documented, standards-based interfaces where practicable, including modern application programming interfaces and recognized health data exchange standards. Describe support for synchronous, asynchronous, event-driven, batch, and secure file exchange patterns, including reconciliation and error handling. Provide interface monitoring, message traceability, retry, alerting, testing, version control, and non-production environments. Allow the Government or a designated third party to integrate, automate, and extract data through appropriately secured interfaces without unnecessary contractual restrictions. Reporting, Analytics, and Data Portability Provide configurable dashboards, recurring reports, ad hoc analysis, data mining, filtering, sorting, alerts, and exports. Support enterprise, regional, facility, service, team, role, and user-level reporting for workload, timeliness, productivity, accuracy, quality, compliance, workflow, and revenue status. Integrate with Government analytics and enterprise data platforms, including common business intelligence tools. Provide complete, documented data dictionaries, lineage, metadata, refresh frequency, retention controls, and historical access. Enable Government-controlled export of transactional, audit, configuration, rule, reference, workflow, and reporting data in open, usable formats without additional extraction fees. Cyber

title: Department of War Office of the Assistant Secretary of War OASW(EI&E) Resilient Infrastructure and Layered Passive Survivability
description: Description. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses to this RFI. It will also not consider any solutions that are proprietary unless clearly marked. Overview. The Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Energy, Installations, and Environment (OASW(EI&E)) is soliciting concepts, capabilities, and technical insights from the military construction (MILCON), materials science, and defense-industrial sectors. The focus areas can be found in the attachment below. The Department of War (DoW) is transitioning its installation framework to support active operational posture. Under Title 10 of the U.S. Code and the strategic directives of the annual National Defense Authorization Act, military installations are recognized as primary power projection platforms. The survivability of these installations under kinetic and multi-domain threats is directly related to the readiness and capabilities of the U.S. Armed Forces. To support the development of the �Base of the Future,� the DoW seeks novel, non-prescriptive solutions in passive force protection to protect physical structures, personnel, and critical utility infrastructures. The Department intends to move past traditional �pour-concrete-and-hope� hardening and pivot the paradigm to focus on minimizing target signature, absorbing kinetic energy dynamically, and maintaining mission-essential functions even during active degradation. The DoW intends to use these insights to actively shape near-term procurement and long-term modernization strategies. Specifically, mature, ready-to-deploy technologies will be evaluated for immediate integration and inclusion in upcoming military construction standards. Promising, early-stage concepts will be used to guide and prioritize future research, development, and science and technology funding pipelines. Background. To identify potential technological advancements, the DoW seeks information categorized into four functional, capability-based domains. Respondents are encouraged to look beyond legacy building codes and focus on facility survivability in contested environments. Disclaimer: This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and strategic planning. This does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it obligate the Office of the Secretary of War or OASW(EI&E) to fund or contract for any submitted concepts.

title: Governor Control Programming
description: Amendment 0001 is issued to extend the Request for Quotation due date from 2 November 2026 to 6 November 2026, 12:00 PM PST. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) at the Libby Dam Project (17877 Hwy 37, Libby, MT 59923) is modernizing its Main Unit Governors by replacing existing pressure switches with pressure transducers on five (5) units. The objective of this contract is to procure specialized governor control programming, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) / Human Machine Interface (HMI) development, and commissioning support from the contractor to accommodate this hardware change. This is a turnkey requirement; the Contractor assumes full responsibility for understanding the existing system logic and delivering a fully functional, updated programming solution with no technical assistance from the Government. Work shall be accomplished on a rolling outage basis as units become available, spanning from the Contract Award Date through August 30, 2027. Work will occur across remote and on-site location, structured as follows: Tasks 1 & 3 (Remote): Contractor's Facility. Task 2 (On-Site Commissioning): Libby Dam Project, 17155 HWY 37, Libby, MT 59923-9703 Quoters must submit a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) quote for all contract line item numbers (CLINs). Incomplete quotes will be ineligible for award. To be considered for award, interested parties must submit an email quote package directly adhering to the following rules: E-mail Address: Quotes must be emailed to the Contract Specialist, Londres Medranda, at londres.medranda@usace.army.mil SAM Registration: Offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of quote submission and maintain it through performance and final payment. Inquiries & Questions: Questions must be sent via email to the Contract Specialist no later than five (5) working days prior to the quote due date. This ensures sufficient time for the Government to publish amendments on SAM.gov.

title: JBMHH Gate Heaters & Fans Supply Rental
description: The Government intends to acquire a contract to provide eight (8) outdoor heaters and eight (8) misting fans, to be exchanged seasonally, for use at the access control points identified in the Specific Tasks section. All units will be operated outdoors and must be suitable for exposure to environmental elements. The Contractor shall provide, emplace, maintain, and recover all equipment. JBMHH will furnish fuel, water, and electricity necessary for operation. The Contractor shall inspect all equipment provided, including ensuring that all electrical cords are adequate and compatible with the required electrical supply. The contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, materials, and technical expertise required to perform diagnostics, repairs, replacements, and stabilization actions. Routine maintenance shall be conducted during standard business hours; however, the contractor must maintain continuous on-call support to respond to critical failures such as electrical hazards, complete equipment shutdown, or conditions that render the gate unsafe or inoperable. All work shall comply with applicable Army, DoD, and installation safety standards, ensuring uninterrupted support to access control operations.

description: NSN 0R-7025-017061785-H1, TDP VER 001, QTY 13 EA, DELIVERY FOB ORIGIN. The design of this part is unstable. Engineering, manufacturing, or performance characteristics indicate that the required design objectives have not been achieved. Major changes are contemplated because the part has a low process yield or has demonstrated marginal performance during tests or service use. These changes will render the present part obsolete and unusable in its present configuration. Limited acquisition/repair from the present source is anticipated pending configuration changes. The subject item requires Government source approval prior to contract award, as the item is flight critical and/or the technical data available has not been determined adequate to support acquisition via full and open competition. Only the source(s) previously approved by the Government for this item have been solicited. The time required for approval of a new source is normally such that an award cannot be delayed pending approval of a new source. If you are not an approved source you must submit, together with your proposal, the information detailed in one of the NAVSUP Weapon Systems Support (NAVSUP WSS) Source Approval Information Brochures listed below. Spares: https://www.navsup.navy.mil/NAVSUP-Enterprise/NAVSUP-Weapon-Systems-Sup port/Business-Opps/ Repair: https://www.navsup.navy.mil/NAVSUP-Enterprise/NAVSUP -Weapon-Systems-Support/Business-Opps/ technical data required to be submitted based on your company's experience in production of the same or similar item, or if this is an item you have never made. If your request for source approval is currently being evaluated at NAVSUP WSS submit with your offer a copy of the cover letter which forwarded your request for source approval. Offers received which fail to provide all data required by the Source Approval Brochure or document previous submission of all data required by the Source Approval Brochure will not be considered for award under this solicitation. Please note, if evaluation of a source approval request submitted hereunder cannot be processed in time and/or approval requirements preclude the ability to obtain subject items in time to meet Government requirements, award of the subject requirement may continue based on Fleet support needs. The NAVSUP WSS Commercial Item Identification Brochure is now available at: "https://www.navsup.navy.mil/NAVSUP-Enterprise/NAVSUP-Weapon-Systems-Support/Bus iness-Opps/" Interested parties may obtain copies of Military and Federal Specificationsand Standards, Qualified Products Lists (QPLs), Qualified Product Databases(QPDs), Military Handbooks, and other standardized documents from the DoDSingle Stock Point (DODSSP) at Document Automation and Production Service(DAPS) in Philadelphia, PA. NOTE: Patterns, Drawings, Deviation Lists, Purchase Descriptions, etc. are NOT stocked at DODSSP. Most documents are available in Adobe PDF format from ASSIST-Online at: http://quicksearch.dla.mil/. Users may use ASSIST-Quick Search to search for and download available documents directly using standard browser software. Documents that are not available for downloading from ASSIST-Quick Search can be ordered from the DODSSP website using the ASSIST Shopping Wizard after obtaining a DODSSP Customer Account by following the registration procedures. Users who do not have access to the internet may contact the DODSSP ASSISTHelp Desk at 215-697-2667 or 215-697-2179 (DSN: 442-2667), or mail their request to DLADocument Services, Bldg. 4/D, 700 Robbins Avenue, Philadelphia PA 19111-5094. All responsible sources may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals, quotationsor capability statements. This notice of intent is not a request forcompetitive proposals. However, all proposals received within 45 days (30days if award is issued under an existing Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) afterdate of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Award will be made only if the offeror, the product/service, or the manufacturer meets the qualification requirement(s) at time of award, in accordance with FAR clause 52.209-1. The solicitation identifies the office where additional information can be obtained concerning qualification requirements and is cited in each individual solicitation. However, interested persons may identify tothe contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy theGovernment's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice.
